Let's now determine the behavior along the axes.

- The straight-line solutions on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-axis have the form ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/a12ab1d3c69a589aa8de66fe8d14ed19b2938a9ef5591d87860e101a95afdc55.svg) Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/3db8d2103adafd2be29df482295b07ef63576be6f152793463e034e808725edf.svg) we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/bb6223675110a379d33203ff637afaa6aefd3edf507b5a93386c608aa7aafca5.svg) as ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/e54727d514ed264e6dd30c7f4044746e6d2b4b462dc3776daecf7eb68634c358.svg) Thus, the trajectories on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-axis move *toward* the origin (*stable axis*).

- The straight-line solutions on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-axis have the form ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/aae0f8015e0a575ca1e1fdbb37d011cbf78574649e3c9874163c3f14f1ca9929.svg) Since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/23d0a8291d49cc1d2f0c6cff735a4d5214c2d9079dca67d803846af9b063358f.svg) we have that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/69c464920e94e968ac5b2fe07f52d5e8a5e694f0fab6c9bfdcfd1b359a82e89e.svg) as ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/e54727d514ed264e6dd30c7f4044746e6d2b4b462dc3776daecf7eb68634c358.svg) Thus, the trajectories on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-axis move *toward* the origin (*stable axis*).

Because both axes are *stable*, the origin (equilibrium point) is called a **stable node** or **sink**.

In the phase portrait, we draw

- arrows on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/fcc5df999e3b49fae1685ee0ab5bd03709804e1dd49f2ee722c4269eb0f5506d.svg)-axis pointing *inward* (toward the origin), and

- arrows on the ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121715/assets/1d9b846cface9f9348e4081a0dd87dd254bf26663c12aa0d1a15aa24d2393261.svg)-axis pointing *inward* (toward the origin).

A typical trajectory flows into the origin.
